statement: In the system of equations below, $a$ and $b$ are constants. $$\begin{aligned} ax + 5y &= 6 \\ 12x + by &= 18 \end{aligned}$$ If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of $a + b$?

choices.misconception: I found $a = 4$ correctly but then divided 5 by 3 for $b$ instead of multiplying, so I got $4 + \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{17}{3}$.
I found $a = 4$ but kept $b = 5$ from the first equation instead of scaling it by 3, so I got $4 + 5 = 9$.
I thought the two equations had to have the same coefficients, so I set $a = 12$ and $b = 5$ and got 17.

hints: Infinitely many solutions means the two equations describe the same line.
Then one equation is a constant multiple of the other. Use the constants on the right side to find that multiple.
Since $18 = 3 \cdot 6$, the second equation is $3$ times the first: $12 = 3a$ and $b = 3 \cdot 5$.

solutions.reliable: For infinitely many solutions the second equation must be a multiple of the first. Comparing the right sides, $18 = 3 \cdot 6$, so the multiple is $3$. Then $3a = 12$ gives $a = 4$, and $b = 3 \cdot 5 = 15$. So $a + b = 19$. Check: $3(4x + 5y) = 12x + 15y$ and $3 \cdot 6 = 18$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
